examples.description: Synthetic teaching example: usable facial evidence, supplied older-portrait chronology and a supported qualitative embedding interpretation.

imageDescriptions.Media-2: EXAMPLE ONLY, not actual pixels: focused near-frontal selfie of a fictional adult in a room, with visible shoulders and no visible display border.

aura.interpretation: The supplied fixture interpretation describes relatively high embedding similarity; it supplies no calibrated identity-acceptance threshold.

observations: Both eyes, the nose outline and mouth are visible in a near-frontal portrait.

apparentAge.basis: Visible facial appearance supports a broad young-adult range.
limitations: Low reference detail makes fine age estimation unreliable.

observations: The whole selfie shows a face, shoulders and a room background; the face is in focus.

apparentAge.basis: Visible facial appearance supports a broad adult range that includes the supplied expected age of 36.
limitations: Appearance varies; this range is not a measurement of chronological age.

evidence: Visible eye contours, nose outline and mouth proportions are compatible with the supplied similarity interpretation.
limitations: These observations do not independently establish identity.

evidence: The supplied dates place the holder at 26 in the reference photo and 36 at selfie capture; the broad apparent-age ranges include those ages.
limitations: The older reference reasonably limits direct comparison of age-related appearance.

indicators.evidence: No display border is visible within the supplied selfie frame.
The selfie does not resolve a surface on which paper texture could be assessed.
One still image supplies no change of viewpoint over time.

observations: The visible room context does not itself prove physical presence or camera authenticity.
limitations: Static absence of a bezel does not rule out display replay or other manipulation.

output.summary: The visible facial details and supplied age chronology support the provided embedding interpretation. The older portrait and still-only capture limit the conclusions; the BFF retains the identity decision.

examples.description: Synthetic teaching example: clear visual differences and a processing cue create tension with a supplied high embedding-similarity interpretation.

imageDescriptions.Media-2: EXAMPLE ONLY, not actual pixels: clear near-frontal fictional adult selfie with broader jaw and mouth, older-looking facial appearance and a visible tonal boundary at the face-background edge.

aura.interpretation: The supplied fixture interpretation describes high embedding similarity; no calibrated identity-acceptance decision accompanies it.

observations: A near-frontal reference shows a narrow jaw contour and a comparatively narrow mouth.

apparentAge.basis: Visible facial appearance supports a broad adult range that includes the supplied reference-photo age of 34.
limitations: Apparent age remains approximate even in a clear portrait.

observations: A near-frontal selfie shows a broader jaw and mouth; a visible tonal boundary crosses the face-background edge.

apparentAge.basis: Visible facial appearance suggests an older adult range than the supplied expected age of 38.
limitations: Lighting, appearance variation or image processing may affect this estimate.

evidence: The visible jaw and mouth differences under similar pose warrant review alongside the supplied high-similarity interpretation.
limitations: Visible differences do not by themselves establish different identities; expression or image processing may contribute.

evidence: The broad selfie appearance estimate does not include the supplied expected age of 38.
limitations: An appearance estimate cannot establish an incorrect DOB or an identity mismatch.

indicators.evidence: A visible tonal boundary at the face-background edge is a candidate processing or compositing cue.
Illumination at that visible edge appears discontinuous with the adjacent background.
A single frame supplies no replay dynamics.

observations: The visible edge could arise from benign processing or capture conditions as well as manipulation.
limitations: These static cues are not a qualified deepfake finding or a live/spoof verdict.

output.summary: The supplied high-similarity interpretation has meaningful visual tension: jaw and mouth appearance differ, the age estimate raises a question, and an edge artifact merits review. None of these observations independently resolves identity or manipulation.
